problem.statement_vernacular: Tired all the time for three months

subjective.vernacular: When exactly did the tiredness start, and did it come on suddenly or gradually?
subjective.why_it_matters: Gradual onset over weeks favors anemia, hypothyroidism, or depression; sudden onset favors infectious or inflammatory causes.
subjective.missing: exact onset date, sudden vs. gradual characterization

subjective.vernacular: How many hours do you sleep, do you feel rested when you wake up, and do you snore or wake up gasping?
subjective.why_it_matters: Poor or non-restorative sleep points toward obstructive sleep apnea, insomnia, or depression as primary drivers of fatigue.

subjective.vernacular: For those who menstruate: are periods heavier than usual, longer, or more frequent?
subjective.why_it_matters: Heavy menstrual bleeding is the most common cause of iron-deficiency anemia, which is already suggested by the low hemoglobin.

subjective.vernacular: Do you follow any special diet, avoid meat or animal products, or have you changed your eating habits recently?
subjective.why_it_matters: Vegetarian or vegan diets restrict iron, B12, and folate, all of which can cause nutritional anemia.

subjective.vernacular: Have you gained or lost weight over the past three to six months without trying?
subjective.why_it_matters: Unintentional weight loss raises concern for malignancy, hyperthyroidism, or chronic inflammatory disease; weight gain supports hypothyroidism.

subjective.vernacular: Do you feel colder than others around you, have dry skin, hair loss, or constipation?
subjective.why_it_matters: These are classic symptoms of hypothyroidism, a common and treatable cause of fatigue that overlaps with anemia.

subjective.vernacular: Have you felt sad, hopeless, or lost interest in things you used to enjoy, and has your concentration or motivation dropped?
subjective.why_it_matters: Depressive disorder is a leading cause of chronic fatigue and can coexist with anemia or thyroid disease.

subjective.vernacular: Do you get short of breath doing things that used to be easy, or notice your heart racing or pounding?
subjective.why_it_matters: Cardiopulmonary symptoms with the known low hemoglobin suggest the anemia is functionally significant and may indicate cardiac or pulmonary comorbidity.

subjective.vernacular: Have you noticed black or tarry stools, bright red blood in the stool, or blood when vomiting?
subjective.why_it_matters: GI blood loss is a major cause of iron-deficiency anemia and can signal serious underlying pathology including colorectal cancer.

subjective.vernacular: What prescription drugs, over-the-counter medicines, or supplements do you take regularly?
subjective.why_it_matters: NSAIDs cause GI blood loss; metformin impairs B12 absorption; many medications cause fatigue directly or through bone marrow suppression.

subjective.vernacular: Have you had fevers, drenching night sweats, or noticed lumps in your neck, armpits, or groin?
subjective.why_it_matters: These B-symptoms raise concern for lymphoma or other hematologic malignancy as the cause of anemia and fatigue.

subjective.vernacular: How much alcohol do you drink in a typical week, and do you use any recreational substances?
subjective.why_it_matters: Alcohol causes macrocytic anemia, liver disease, poor nutrition, and fatigue through multiple mechanisms.

objective.vernacular: The amount of oxygen-carrying protein in the blood — low means anemia

objective.term: Complete blood count with differential and indices (MCV, MCH, RDW)
objective.vernacular: Full red and white blood cell panel including cell size and shape markers
The body's main iron storage protein — low confirms iron deficiency
Tests that show how much iron is circulating and how much the blood can carry
A pituitary hormone that shows whether the thyroid is working too slowly or too fast
Panel checking kidney function, liver enzymes, blood sugar, and electrolytes
Blood levels of two vitamins essential for making healthy red blood cells
Measures young red blood cells to show whether the bone marrow is responding to anemia

objective.term: Erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR) and C-reactive protein (CRP)
objective.vernacular: Inflammation markers — elevated levels suggest the body is fighting something

objective.term: Physical examination: pallor, heart rate, blood pressure
objective.vernacular: Checking whether skin and mucous membranes look pale, and whether pulse and blood pressure are normal

objective.term: Physical examination: thyroid gland palpation and lymphadenopathy
objective.vernacular: Feeling the neck for an enlarged thyroid or swollen lymph nodes

objective.term: Fecal occult blood test (FOBT) or fecal immunochemical test (FIT)
objective.vernacular: A stool sample test that detects hidden blood not visible to the naked eye
A nine-question validated questionnaire that scores the severity of depression symptoms

assessment_candidates.vernacular: The body's iron stores are too low to make enough healthy red blood cells, causing tiredness
assessment_candidates.basis: Hemoglobin 11.2 g/dL is consistent with mild-to-moderate anemia; iron deficiency is the most prevalent cause of anemia worldwide, especially in menstruating persons and those with poor dietary intake or GI blood loss.
assessment_candidates.confidence_note: Likely based on hemoglobin alone, but cannot confirm without ferritin, MCV, and iron studies; anemia of chronic disease can produce identical hemoglobin values.
assessment_candidates.severity_vernacular: Treatable with iron supplementation once confirmed, but the underlying cause of iron loss (e.g., GI bleeding, heavy periods) must be found to prevent recurrence.

assessment_candidates.term: Anemia of chronic disease / anemia of inflammation
assessment_candidates.vernacular: A chronic illness or ongoing inflammation is suppressing the body's ability to make red blood cells
assessment_candidates.basis: Anemia of chronic disease is common in the presence of autoimmune, inflammatory, infectious, or neoplastic conditions; it typically produces normocytic or mildly microcytic anemia with normal or elevated ferritin.
assessment_candidates.confidence_note: Cannot distinguish from iron deficiency anemia without full iron studies and inflammatory markers; these two conditions can also coexist.
assessment_candidates.severity_vernacular: Depends entirely on the underlying cause — an autoimmune disease is manageable, but an undiagnosed malignancy causing chronic anemia carries serious risk if found late.

assessment_candidates.vernacular: The thyroid gland is underactive and not making enough hormone, slowing down the whole body and causing fatigue
not_yet_testable: s-006 (cold intolerance/constipation symptoms — not yet gathered)
assessment_candidates.basis: Hypothyroidism is a common, easily tested, and treatable cause of subacute fatigue; it can also directly cause a normocytic anemia, making it relevant to both the fatigue and the low hemoglobin.
assessment_candidates.confidence_note: No TSH has been drawn; cannot assess likelihood until thyroid function is tested.
assessment_candidates.severity_vernacular: Highly treatable with daily thyroid hormone replacement once diagnosed; unaddressed it causes worsening fatigue, cognitive slowing, and cardiovascular risk over years.

assessment_candidates.vernacular: A mood disorder that causes persistent low energy, sadness, and loss of interest — and is a leading cause of chronic fatigue
not_yet_testable: s-007 (mood and neurovegetative symptoms — not yet gathered)
assessment_candidates.basis: Depression is one of the most common causes of fatigue lasting more than one month in primary care; it frequently coexists with medical illness including anemia.
assessment_candidates.confidence_note: No psychiatric screening has been performed; fatigue alone is insufficient to diagnose depression, but the symptom overlap requires systematic screening.
assessment_candidates.severity_vernacular: Untreated depression causes lasting impairment in function, relationships, and quality of life, and carries risk of self-harm if severe.

assessment_candidates.vernacular: Low levels of B12 or folate cause the body to make large, poorly functioning red blood cells, leading to fatigue
assessment_candidates.basis: B12 and folate deficiency produce macrocytic anemia and fatigue; risk is elevated in vegans, the elderly, and those on metformin or proton pump inhibitors.
assessment_candidates.confidence_note: MCV is unknown; if MCV is elevated, this candidate moves substantially up the list.
assessment_candidates.severity_vernacular: B12 deficiency can cause irreversible neurological damage if untreated for an extended period, even after the anemia is corrected.

assessment_candidates.vernacular: Breathing repeatedly stops during sleep, preventing truly restful sleep and causing daytime exhaustion
not_yet_testable: s-002 (sleep quality and snoring — not yet gathered)
assessment_candidates.basis: OSA is a prevalent and underdiagnosed cause of persistent fatigue; it can coexist with anemia and does not cause it, but both conditions can be present simultaneously.
assessment_candidates.confidence_note: No sleep history has been gathered; body habitus, snoring history, and witnessed apneas are needed to assess pre-test probability.
assessment_candidates.severity_vernacular: Untreated severe OSA raises long-term risk of hypertension, cardiac arrhythmia, and stroke.

assessment_candidates.vernacular: A cancer of the blood or lymph system that impairs normal blood cell production and causes fatigue and anemia
not_yet_testable: o-002 (CBC with differential — not yet ordered)
assessment_candidates.basis: Anemia plus subacute fatigue warrants exclusion of hematologic malignancy; a peripheral blood smear and full CBC with differential are the critical initial steps.
assessment_candidates.confidence_note: Low prior probability in the general population but severity class I mandates it remain on the list until the CBC and clinical picture are complete.
assessment_candidates.severity_vernacular: Hematologic malignancies are life-threatening; delayed diagnosis significantly worsens outcomes.

residual.vernacular: Something not on this list — the differential is never closed

plan_options.term: Iron studies panel: serum ferritin, serum iron, TIBC, transferrin saturation
plan_options.vernacular: Blood tests to confirm or rule out iron deficiency as the cause of the low hemoglobin
plan_options.basis: Iron studies are the first-line workup for anemia with unknown etiology; ferritin below 30 ng/mL confirms iron deficiency with high specificity.

plan_options.term: Complete blood count with differential and red cell indices
plan_options.vernacular: Full blood count including cell size and type breakdown to characterize the anemia
plan_options.basis: MCV, RDW, and differential help distinguish iron deficiency (microcytic, high RDW) from B12/folate deficiency (macrocytic) from anemia of chronic disease (normocytic).

plan_options.vernacular: A single blood test that reliably screens for both underactive and overactive thyroid
plan_options.basis: TSH is the recommended first-line screening test for thyroid dysfunction per American Thyroid Association guidelines.

plan_options.term: Serum vitamin B12 and RBC folate
plan_options.vernacular: Blood tests for two vitamins essential to healthy red blood cell production
plan_options.basis: Recommended when MCV is elevated or dietary risk factors for deficiency are present; B12 deficiency also causes neurological damage requiring prompt treatment.

plan_options.term: ESR, CRP, and comprehensive metabolic panel
plan_options.vernacular: Inflammation markers and organ function tests to look for a hidden chronic illness causing the anemia
plan_options.basis: Elevated ESR/CRP with normocytic anemia points toward anemia of chronic disease and triggers further search for autoimmune, infectious, or neoplastic cause.

plan_options.vernacular: A validated nine-question depression questionnaire completed by the patient
plan_options.basis: PHQ-9 has sensitivity ~88% and specificity ~88% for major depressive disorder; recommended by USPSTF for adults in primary care.
plan_options.who_can_act: any trained clinical staff member or self-administered

plan_options.vernacular: A stool test to check for hidden blood that could be causing iron-deficiency anemia through GI bleeding
plan_options.basis: Recommended for occult GI blood loss workup in anemia; positive result warrants colonoscopy referral especially in adults over 45.
plan_options.who_can_act: ordering clinician; patient collects sample at home

plan_options.vernacular: A pathologist examines blood cells under the microscope for abnormal shapes or immature cells suggesting bone marrow disease
plan_options.basis: Indicated when CBC suggests dysplastic or abnormal cells; essential to exclude hematologic malignancy before attributing anemia to a benign cause.
